nameOrigin.text: Named for the prominent butte overlooking the area.

founded.text: Platted on April 25, 1874, on land Jeremiah Gould homesteaded in 1869

timeline.text: Locals pushed for a railroad depot in Castle Rock, the designated seat of the newly realigned Douglas County.
A depot of rhyolite stone went up on Third Street on the Denver & Rio Grande line.
The Castle Rock Chamber of Commerce created the Starlighting celebration.
The depot was moved to 420 Elbert Street.
The Castle Rock Historical Society opened the Castle Rock Museum in the depot in October.

sites.name: Castle Rock Museum
sites.hours: Wednesday–Friday noon–5 pm; Saturday 11 am–4 pm

trails.name: Castlewood Canyon State Park
trails.size: 2,628 acres of the Black Forest region, with 12 miles of trails and 60-foot rock-climbing walls
trails.address: 2989 South State Highway 83, Franktown. The main (east) entrance is off Highway 83 five miles south of Franktown; the west entrance is off Castlewood Canyon Road from Highway 86.
trails.season: Sunrise to sunset. The visitor center is open Wednesday to Sunday, 9 am–5 pm. CPW lists no closures.
trails.dogs: On a leash. Service animals and horses are also allowed.
trails.fee: Daily vehicle pass $10–$12 with Colorado plates, $15–$17 out of state (its summary says $10–$15); $4 a person on foot, bike or horseback; annual vehicle pass $80, or the $29 Keep Colorado Wild Pass with Colorado vehicle registration.
